source: examples/baseline-comparison (event poster)
brief: A poster for a neighbourhood jazz night on Friday 14 March at The Lantern, 8pm, free entry.
without: A poster for a neighbourhood jazz night on Friday 14 March at The Lantern, 8pm, free entry.
with: Event poster, portrait 3:4. Text, exactly and only: 'Neighbourhood Jazz Night', 'Friday 14 March', '8pm', 'The Lantern', 'Free entry'. No other words, no address, no slogans, no logos. Hierarchy: the title largest, top left; then date and time; then the venue; 'Free entry' smallest. Two typefaces only: a high-contrast serif for the title and a plain sans for the facts. All text sits on calm, flat areas of dark sky with strong contrast, with generous, even margins. Image: a quiet city street at night, one warm street lamp as the only light source, a double bass leaning in the lamp's pool of light with clear space between the bass and the lamp post; the lamp at true street-lamp height next to the bass. Value plan: dark blue night, the lit pool the brightest area and the focal point, nothing else competing. Palette: deep navy and blue-black with warm amber light and cream, at most three hues. Painterly but clean surfaces: no grain, no speckle, no sparkles, no lens flare.

Spell the web address exactly. No other words. Hierarchy: 'Moth Night' largest; then the date and time; then the meeting point; the booking line smallest but readable.
